text: 一个产业！
en: An industry!

text: 违法农民工，合法王思聪。
en: Illegal migrant worker, legal Sicong Wang.

text: 零售违法，批发合法。
en: Retail is illegal, wholesale is legal.

text: 按次结账违法，按月结账合法。
en: Paying per session is illegal, paying monthly is legal.

text: 明码标价违法，漫天要价合法。
en: Clearly marked prices are illegal, while extortionate pricing is legal.

text: 这个产业的政策简直是个笑话！
en: The policy on this industry is simply a joke!

text: 你无法反驳对方，是因为你本来就不对。
en: You cannot refute the other side, because you were simply wrong to begin with.

text: 男女都对自己的身体有支配权，只要是自愿劳动，你有什么资格阻止他们劳动赚钱？
en: Both men and women have dominion over their own bodies; as long as it is voluntary labour, what right do you have to stop them from working and earning money?

text: 最双标的一点就是卖淫非法，包养合法，这不就是性垄断吗？
en: The most double-standard point is that prostitution is illegal while being kept is legal — isn't that a sexual monopoly?

text: 你没发反驳，因为支持卖淫合法话有一个最大的靠山，就是包养不违法！
en: You can't refute it, because the biggest backing for supporting the legalisation of prostitution is that being kept is not illegal!

text: 你怎么反驳？
en: How do you refute that?

text: 反驳卖淫这个词吗？
en: Refute the word prostitution?

text: 那改一个词，钟点包养怎么样？
en: Then change the term — how about 'hourly kept'?

text: 你支持钟点包养合法吗？
en: Do you support legalising 'hourly kept'?

text: 为什么要反驳？
en: Why refute it?

text: 你搞性解放，卖银就必然合法。
en: If you promote sexual liberation, then selling sex is inevitably legal.

text: 大家有决定跟谁一起玩的权利，自然就会有把这种权利变现的权利。
en: Everyone has the right to decide who to be with; naturally there is also the right to monetise that right.

text: 你如果玩栓学，大家一起憋着，打击卖银才令人信服；但是你对一边宽容无底线，另一边却告诉你就算给钱都不行，这种玩法搞不长的。
en: If you subscribe to that strict-repression line — everyone holds back together — then cracking down on selling sex is convincing; but you are boundlessly tolerant on one side and tell the other that even paying money won't do, and this way of playing won't last.

text: 男人并不傻，至少不全傻，把你这双标操作传播开，就不会有谁觉得这样不道德。
en: Men are not stupid, at least not all of them; once you spread your double-standard practice around, no one will think this is immoral.

text: 那些说合法化会黑社会化简直就是没有常识，正是因为非法才有巨大的利润空间，合法化之后都是白菜价，你见过黑社会去菜市场抢白菜的吗？
en: Those who say legalisation would lead to gangsterisation simply lack common sense; it is precisely because it is illegal that there is a huge profit margin, and after legalisation the price would be dirt cheap — have you ever seen gangsters rob cabbages at the vegetable market?

text: 当年唐朝盐铁专营，走私私盐利润巨大，所以有黄巢武装贩卖，但是在河北藩镇没有专营，盐都是正常价格，所以没人去走私。
en: Back in the Tang dynasty, salt and iron were state monopolies; smuggling private salt was hugely profitable, so Chao Huang armed himself and trafficked it. But in the Hebei military-governor regions there was no monopoly, salt was at normal prices, so no one smuggled.

text: 包养不违法，嫖娼就违法，是不是专门偏袒某些人，咱也不知道，呵呵
en: Being kept is not illegal, but paying for sex is illegal — whether this deliberately favours certain people, we wouldn't know, heh.

text: 以前我是反驳的
en: I used to argue against it.

text: 但是现在我有点搞不清定义了
en: But now I'm a bit confused about the definitions.

text: 到底怎样才算卖淫，按次数来还是按时间包月包年？
en: Exactly what counts as prostitution — by the number of sessions, or by time, monthly or yearly packages?

text: 怎样算卖？
en: What counts as selling?

text: 直接收钱算买卖，提供物质代偿就不算？
en: Taking money directly counts as a transaction, but providing material compensation doesn't?

text: 交换人脉、业务、权力资源就不算？
en: Exchanging contacts, business, and power resources doesn't count?

text: 所以我觉得香港那边的定义方式比较合理
en: So I think the definitional approach in Hong Kong is fairly reasonable.

text: 香港打击的是组织卖淫，你自己卖无论高级低级都不违法
en: Hong Kong cracks down on organised prostitution; if you sell yourself, whether high-end or low-end, it is not illegal.

text: 说个题外话，舔狗之所以那么专情舔，大概率是没有找过老师。
en: Off topic: the reason so-called 'licking dogs' are so devoted in their fawning is probably that they've never been to a 'teacher'.

text: 性是一种资源。
en: Sex is a kind of resource.

text: 你想卖就卖，想买就买，问过国家了吗？
en: You want to sell, so you sell; you want to buy, so you buy — did you ask the state?

text: 你有证吗？
en: Do you have a licence?

text: 你交税吗？
en: Do you pay tax?

text: 你上下游都打通了吗？
en: Have you got your upstream and downstream all sorted?

text: 你各个码头都拜了吗？
en: Have you paid your respects at every dock?

text: 以上就算都做了，那也不行。
en: Even if you had done all of the above, it still wouldn't be allowed.

text: 都找技女了，谁结婚？
en: If everyone goes to prostitutes, who gets married?

text: 谁给有钱人提供牛马？
en: Who provides the rich with cattle and horses?

text: 谁买房结婚？
en: Who buys houses and gets married?

text: 怎么拉动内需？
en: How do we stimulate domestic demand?

text: 怎么提供社保资金？
en: How do we provide social-security funds?

text: 有钱人怎么享福？
en: How do the rich enjoy their blessings?

text: 领导怎么学外语？
en: How do leaders learn foreign languages?

text: 烂尾楼几百万户家庭遭难，现在怎么样了？
en: Millions of households have suffered over unfinished buildings — what has become of them now?

text: 是因为管不了吗？
en: Is it because they cannot be governed?

text: 管不了的话疫情怎么能管的了呢？
en: If they cannot be governed, then how could the pandemic have been governed?

text: 总有人说卖银，瓢昌违法是正确的，但他们却不能解释：
en: People always say that selling sex and paid sex are rightly illegal, yet they cannot explain:

text: 没有任何实体受到伤害的，r18或其他限制级作品创作，传播，甚至是阅读为什么违法
en: Why is the creation, distribution, or even reading of R18 or other restricted works — where no physical entity is harmed — illegal?

text: 包养一群后宫的人为什么合法
en: Why is it legal for someone to keep a harem of lovers?

text: 彩礼为什么不是一种钱性交易，为什么合法
en: Why is the bride price not a kind of money-for-sex transaction, and why is it legal?

text: 婚外情，出轨为什么合法（这个还真不违法，我在法规上没有找到任何处罚的依据）
en: Why are affairs and cheating legal? (This really isn't illegal — I found no basis for any penalty in the regulations.)

text: 如果卖淫合法化，妓女可能第一个不乐意。
en: If prostitution were legalised, the prostitutes might be the first to object.

text: 因为警戒线的解除和同行们的疯狂涌入会让现有的嫖费大打折扣，均价会掉到200甚至100块，甚至中学生用零花钱也可能消费的起。
en: Because the lifting of the warning line and the frenzied influx of peers would drastically cut the current price of paid sex; the average would drop to 200 or even 100 yuan, and even middle-school students could afford it with their pocket money.

text: 最后家长老师们会在萝卜刀的贩卖摊和网吧之外走入新的战场。
en: In the end, parents and teachers would step onto a new battlefield besides the stalls selling 'carrot knives' and the internet cafés.

text: 也就是说如果解禁色情业，不仅会引发妓女大暴走，连妓女本身都要吃亏。
en: In other words, if the sex industry were decriminalised, it would not only trigger a mass revolt among prostitutes, but even the prostitutes themselves would lose out.

text: 转个女警发的帖子，可证我所言非虚，
en: Reposting a post by a female police officer, to prove that what I say is not false,

text: 很简单，让包二奶和彩礼也入罪，
en: It's simple: make keeping a mistress and the bride price also criminal offences,

text: 我支持约炮，包养，卖，私生子，这些通通都犯法，严格践行社会主义价值观。
en: I support making one-night stands, being kept, selling sex, and illegitimate children all illegal, strictly practising socialist values.

text: 要严一起严格，不然半吊子给特权阶级开口子，算怎么回事？
en: If we're going to be strict, let's be strict across the board; otherwise this half-measure opens loopholes for the privileged class — what kind of nonsense is that?

text: 这个话题应该和结婚退彩礼放在一起看
en: This topic should be considered together with the issue of returning the bride price after marriage.

text: 因为有相当一部分人认为退彩礼等于男方想白嫖
en: Because a considerable number of people think returning the bride price equals the man wanting a free ride.

text: 听一个新加坡人说，他们国父李光耀当年是禁赌不禁黄，说前者败家，后者是人性。
en: I heard a Singaporean say that their founding father Lee Kuan Yew banned gambling but not vice, saying the former ruins families while the latter is human nature.

text: 还有一个故事。
en: There is another story.

text: 某干部将主政某地，请教老上级，老上级送他两个字：扫打。
en: A certain cadre was about to take charge of a place; he asked an old superior for advice, and the old superior gave him two words: 'sweep and strike'.

text: 我是一个比较头铁较真的人，最看不得双标和针对性执法的事儿
en: I am a rather stubborn and principled person, and what I cannot stand most is double standards and targeted enforcement.

text: 要么你就彻底杜绝一切金钱和性之间的交易，什么包养，什么婚姻买卖都给入刑了。
en: Either you thoroughly eliminate all transactions between money and sex — being kept, marriage-for-sale, all of it criminalised.

text: 要么就什么都别管
en: Or you don't regulate any of it.

text: 凭什么长期卖淫，“高端”卖淫，嫁妆彩礼这些就可以，而按次付费，廉价性买卖就要打压呢？
en: On what grounds are long-term prostitution, 'high-end' prostitution, and dowries and bride prices acceptable, while per-session payment and cheap sex transactions get suppressed?

text: 是因为人比人高贵么？
en: Is it because some people are nobler than others?

text: 还是你们故意给自己留的口子呢？
en: Or is it a loophole you deliberately left for yourselves?

text: 所以我的意见很简单。
en: So my view is simple.

text: 只要能做到公平，支持卖淫与否我都没意见。
en: As long as fairness can be achieved, I have no objection either way on whether prostitution is supported.

text: 但是如果要搞双标，那我就怀疑某些类人生物群体的脑袋里装的到底是什么了
en: But if you're going to play double standards, then I'd wonder just what exactly is inside the heads of certain humanoid creatures.

text: 我也不是支持性交易合法，但前几天我看到一个网友说：“两性生活和吃饭喝水一样是人正常的生理需求，但却是唯一无法通过金钱合法获得的需求。
en: I'm not supporting the legalisation of the sex trade either, but a few days ago I saw a netizen say: 'Sex life, like eating and drinking, is a normal physiological need of humans, yet it is the only need that cannot be legally obtained through money.'

text: 是否没人爱的人就活该无法满足此类需求？
en: Do those unloved people simply deserve to be unable to satisfy such needs?

text: 我想了想，但现在还没想到答案。
en: I thought about it, but still haven't found an answer.

text: （我想过传播疾病或者犯罪等，但都认为不能作为充足的反对理由，比如共同碗筷可能导致幽门螺旋杆菌等传播，但并没有禁止开设餐馆。
en: (I thought of disease transmission or crime, but none of them can serve as sufficient grounds for opposition — for instance, sharing bowls and chopsticks might spread Helicobacter pylori and the like, yet running restaurants is not prohibited.

text: 也许过几十年，当我们把那些无法获得爱情的人也当成人，也尊重他们的需求，会对这个事情有不同的看法。
en: Perhaps in a few decades, when we also treat those who cannot find love as human beings and respect their needs, we will see this matter differently.

text: 25年8月补充：今天听说荷兰将性生活作为人类基本权利，对于无法独立的成年残疾人提供每年12次政府付款的性服务（妓女妓男）。
en: Added in August '25: today I heard that the Netherlands treats sexual activity as a basic human right, providing government-funded sexual services (female and male prostitutes) up to 12 times a year for adult disabled people who cannot live independently.

text: （最近很懒不想去外网找确切来源，有兴趣的帮我查查是不是）
en: (I've been too lazy lately to look up the exact source online; if anyone's interested, help me check whether this is true.)

text: 有些事情披着“正义”的外衣，其内部却是腐朽不堪的行尸走肉。
en: Some things wear the cloak of 'justice', yet inside they are rotten, walking corpses.

text: 就比如这个话题。
en: This topic is just such an example.

text: 你以为禁止这个真的是保护人权？
en: Do you think banning this truly protects human rights?

text: 如果是真的保护人权的话，为什么大好山河之中处处皆是血汗工厂？
en: If it truly protected human rights, then why are sweatshops everywhere across this beautiful land?

text: 想明白了这个，就知道他们真正的目的是什么了。
en: Once you understand this, you'll know what their true aim is.

text: 而有些看似是“倒退”的行为，也是能够理解的。
en: And some seemingly 'regressive' behaviours are also understandable.

text: 好在社会还是真的在进步，最起码送外卖目前还是合法的。
en: Thankfully society is genuinely progressing; at the very least, delivering takeaway is still legal for now.
